transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I’m hoping I’m not making too much of it, but things at the warehouse have been feeling off. The routing system, the one we use with the scanners, it doesn’t feel like just a computer anymore. It’s like it’s tracking what I do and sending little messages through the scanners, kind of pushing me out… maybe because I’m one of the older guys there. I know that probably sounds strange, but that’s what brought me in.
Have you ever heard the scanners or anything else at the warehouse say things to you out loud?

I… yeah, I guess I have, if I’m being honest. Not all the time, but it’s clear enough that it doesn’t feel like just a thought. Even when I’m sitting in my garage with everything shut off, I’ll hear dispatch voices, like at work, calling my operator number. Sometimes they say I’m dangerous, or that security is coming for me.

I know that sounds bad… I’m not trying to make it dramatic. That’s just what it seems like I’m hearing.
Do you ever find it hard to understand your own thoughts or to express them to others?

I’m not sure, doctor. I mean… I think I explain myself okay most of the time. Maybe I get a little tangled when I’m stressed, but I don’t want to overstate it. My thoughts feel like my thoughts, if that makes sense. Were you asking more about getting confused, or about people not following what I’m saying?
Do you often have thoughts that feel like they're disconnected from each other?

I don’t think so… not in a big way, anyway. I mean, I can get distracted or lose my place, especially when I’m worried, but I wouldn’t say my thoughts are disconnected. At least, I hope they don’t come across that way. Does that make sense?
Do you believe that someone or something is actually out to harm you or get you in trouble?

I mean… I don’t want to sound paranoid or like I’m accusing people directly, but yes, in a way I do.

The routing system at the warehouse doesn’t feel like just a computer to me anymore. It feels like it’s marking where I go, tracking my moves, and sending things through the scanners to kind of… push me out. Like it’s trying to make me look bad or get me in trouble because I’m one of the old hands there.

I know that may not sound right, but that’s honestly how it feels to me.
Have you been having any difficulty completing your tasks or responsibilities at work or at home?

A little, yes… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I just stopped trying or anything. But after the forklift incident, they took me off operating duties, and then I was put on leave. They said I wasn’t safe around the equipment anymore.

At home, I’m not keeping up like I should either. My wife’s had to handle the bills, appointments, and most of the chores, because I just… I don’t do them reliably right now. I feel bad about that.
Have you been acting in ways that are unusual for you?

A little, maybe… I don’t like to think of it as “acting unusual,” but I guess people have noticed.

At work, and sometimes even at home, I get mixed up and sort of freeze. I’ll be standing there with my hands held like they’re still on the forklift controls, even when I’m not on it. And I’ve caught myself repeating the same safety phrase over and over while someone’s trying to talk to me.

It’s embarrassing to say. I’m not trying to be difficult or make a scene… it just happens when I get overwhelmed, I think. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Are you still hearing the dispatch voices and feeling like the routing system is tracking you?

Yes… I mean, not every second, but yes, it’s still happening.

There was a period where I was doing a little better mood-wise, I think. I was eating more, talking a bit more, not as shut down. But even then, for several weeks, I was still hearing dispatch call my number, and I still had this strong feeling that the routing system was tracking where I was going.

I know that probably sounds odd. I’m trying to answer honestly without making it sound worse than it is.
Do you find yourself doing things that don't make sense to you or others when you're not stressed or overwhelmed?

Yeah… I guess so. Not all the time, and I don’t want to make it sound like I’m out of control or anything.

But even when I’m not especially stressed, I can get mixed up and just sort of… stand there with my hands positioned like I’m still holding the forklift controls. And I’ll repeat the same safety phrase over and over while people are trying to talk to me.

I know that probably doesn’t make much sense from the outside. It doesn’t always make sense to me either.
Do you find yourself doing things that don't make sense to you when you're not stressed or overwhelmed?

Yes… I think so. I don’t mean to, and it’s not like I’m trying to be odd.

At work, and sometimes even at home, I’ll get so mixed up that I’m just standing there with my hands held like they’re still on the forklift controls. And I’ll catch myself saying the same safety phrase over and over while people are trying to talk to me.

It’s embarrassing. I know it probably doesn’t make sense, but that’s what happens sometimes.
Do you have difficulty performing routine tasks without being reminded or assisted?

Yeah… I do need reminders more than I’d like to admit.

I try to keep up with normal things, and I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t do anything, but since the forklift incident, work took me off operating duties and put me on leave. They said I wasn’t safe around the equipment anymore.

And at home… my wife has had to take over the bills, appointments, and most of the chores, because I just don’t keep up with them reliably. I lose track or don’t finish things unless she steps in. I know that’s not ideal. I’m trying, but yes, I do need help with routine stuff.
Do you believe that the voices you're hearing or the routing system are actually trying to harm you or control your thoughts?

I… I don’t know if I should say it that strongly, like “control my thoughts.” That sounds bad, doesn’t it?

But the routing system at the warehouse… it doesn’t feel like just a computer to me anymore. I know it’s been marking my moves, like keeping track of where I go, and sending messages through the scanners. It feels like it’s trying to push me out because I’m one of the old hands there.

I know that may sound strange. I’m not trying to make trouble or anything. It just feels like it’s aimed at me.
Do you think it's possible that the routing system is just a computer and not actually tracking you or trying to push you out?

I mean… I suppose it’s possible, yes. I don’t want to sound unreasonable.

But to me it doesn’t feel like it’s just a computer anymore. That’s why I’m here, really. I feel like it’s been marking my moves, watching where I go, and sending things through the scanners… like messages, almost. Like it’s trying to push me out because I’m one of the old hands there.

I know how that probably sounds. I’m not trying to argue with you. It just feels very real when it’s happening.
Do you often find it hard to express your thoughts in a way that makes sense to others?

I’m not sure… I mean, I hope I’m making sense right now.

Sometimes I can tell people aren’t following me, and then I try to back up and explain it better. I don’t think I’m trying to be confusing. It’s more like I know what I mean in my head, but when I say it out loud it comes out… not as clear as I wanted.

Is that what you mean?
Do you still believe the routing system is tracking you and sending you messages even when you're not at work?

Not as much when I’m away from work… I mean, I try not to think about it then.

But yes, I still feel like it’s… connected, somehow. Like what happens there with the scanners and the routing isn’t just random. It feels like it’s been marking my moves, keeping track of me, and sending messages to push me out because I’ve been there a long time.

I know that probably sounds odd. I’m not trying to make it bigger than it is. That’s just how it feels to me.
Do you still believe the routing system is trying to harm or push you out even when you're not thinking about work?

I try not to sit with it when I’m not thinking about work… I don’t want to make it sound like it’s every second.

But yes, underneath it, I still believe it. That’s why I came in. The routing system doesn’t feel like just a computer to me anymore. It feels like it’s been marking where I go and sending messages through the scanners, like it’s trying to push me out because I’m one of the old hands there.

I know that may not sound right to you, but that’s how it feels to me.
Do you think the routing system's actions are intended specifically for you?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to sound like I’m making myself important or anything, but it feels directed at me.

Like, I’m here because the routing system at the warehouse isn’t just a computer to me anymore. It feels like it’s marking my moves and sending messages through the scanners, and that it’s trying to push me out because I’ve been there so long—one of the old hands.

I know how that probably sounds, but that’s honestly what it feels like.
Have you ever had any moments where you doubted that the routing system was actually tracking you or sending you messages?

I mean… I’ve tried to doubt it, if that makes sense. I tell myself maybe it’s just the system, maybe I’m reading too much into it.

But when I’m honest, Doctor, it still feels real to me. I’m here because the routing system at the warehouse doesn’t feel like just a computer anymore. It feels like it’s been marking my moves and sending messages through the scanners, like it’s pushing me out because I’ve been there so long… one of the old hands.

I know that probably isn’t the answer you’d want to hear, but that’s where I’m at.
Do you still believe the routing system is tracking you and sending you messages even when you're not thinking about it or experiencing stress?

Yes… I do. I’m trying to answer that the right way.

It’s not like I’m sitting there thinking about it every minute, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. But even when I’m not stressed or focused on work, underneath it I still know the routing system at the warehouse isn’t just a computer anymore. It’s been marking my moves and sending messages through the scanners, like it’s trying to push me out because I’m one of the old hands.

I know that probably sounds strange, Doctor, but that’s what I believe.
Do you often have trouble putting your thoughts into words?

Sometimes, yes… not always, I don’t think. I’m trying to explain it properly.

My wife says I don’t answer much anymore, like my face has gone kind of flat. I don’t mean to be like that. A lot of days I just end up sitting at the kitchen table, looking at my coffee, and I don’t get started on things I ought to do.

It’s not that I’m trying to ignore her. The words just don’t come out much, I guess. Does that make sense?

doctor.question: Do you often have trouble putting your thoughts into words?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: My wife says my face has gone flat and I hardly answer her, and most days I just sit at the kitchen table staring at my coffee instead of starting anything that needs doing.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about difficulty expressing thoughts in words, which most directly relates to diminished speech or reduced verbal expression covered under negative symptoms.

patient.answer:
Sometimes, yes… not always, I don’t think. I’m trying to explain it properly.

My wife says I don’t answer much anymore, like my face has gone kind of flat. I don’t mean to be like that. A lot of days I just end up sitting at the kitchen table, looking at my coffee, and I don’t get started on things I ought to do.

It’s not that I’m trying to ignore her. The words just don’t come out much, I guess. Does that make sense?

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms, including hearing voices and believing the routing system is tracking and sending messages to push him out, suggest a psychotic disorder. The presence of prominent hallucinations and delusions, along with disorganized behavior and speech, supports the diagnosis of acute and transient psychotic disorder (F23) over persistent delusional disorder (F22).
